newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals edge above earlier fresh lows.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals edge above earlier fresh lows.

text.p: Precious metals prices were barely edging above the recent lows struck across the board on Thursday as the market continued to see thin, uncertain business.

Gold fixed at $372.20 per ounce in the morning, the lowest setting since April 25, 1994, and with the U.S. markets closed until Monday for Thanksgiving, there was little new momentum to lift the price.
Gold's afternoon fix was a fractionally firmer $372.65.
"If it can bounce before the U.S. markets come back on Monday, it could stabilise. Otherwise we could see another bout of selling," one analyst said.
The fix came down from $373.00 on Wednesday on speculator selling and sales by Australian and South African producers.
"A hefty fall in the Dow, or the dollar coming off will be needed to get some interest in gold again," one dealer said.
Dealers said the market had been losing ground all week as the professionals squared off their positions ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday which shuts the U.S. markets until Monday.
"It could be quite thin until then but if somebody tries a move, the lack of market participants will exaggerate it," one dealer said.
Market confidence has been shaken recently by comments from central banks and institutions all of which suggested a more pro-active role for gold reserves was on the long-term agenda.
Analysts estimate the central banks and other institutions hold over 35,000 tonnes of gold in their reserves, the vast majority of which is inactive and kept well away from the market
"These structural movements in thinking have made the market nervous and rightly so," one analyst said.

Another sign of nerves has been reported selling of metal by gold miners from South Africa and Australia where due to strengthening local currencies, domestioc gold prices have been falling even faster than on the international market.
"The producers seem to have decided this is not just a blip but that the price will continue to fall," said bullion analyst Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland.
The other precious metals were also struggling at lower levels on Thursday.
Platinum and palladium prices weakened to fresh lows since 1993 after Japanese Finance Ministry data showed October imports were down by 28.8 and 26.9 percent respectively.
Platinum was down $1.50 at $374.25/$375.25 and palladium ws down $1.00 at $114.00/$115.00. Silver prices were relatively unscathed and unchanged from Wednesday at $4.73/$4.75.
